Reddit's recent shenanigans is likely fulfilling multiple agendas - but one agenda (attracting investors, getting rid of bad PR ) is something that should be wanted across the board for all platforms.

I know Atko has plenty of donations for now, but I'd like VOAT to be a long term success story.

In order to make this happen, we need to work on our public image. VOAT needs a positive reputation. Plenty of half assed slam articles have already been written, but lets make those much harder to write.

In order to do this, I propose we have a default setting when you have a new account - viewing offensive content is disabled. It would also be disabled for any visitors to the site by default (no user account). Now what is offensive? That's a great question, and something that we'd have to consider on a subverse by subverse basis, debating it in a subverse, where the community votes.

So, in the options menu, we have that flag turned off, and you can turn it on. Uncheck disable offensive content. We then pop up a panel that says "are you sure you want to view offensive content? Do you have thick enough skin? Chances are, you will get offended at some point. Keep in mind you are now considered a user account that is actively seeking out content that can be considered offensive to others. Don't say we didn't warn you." Perhaps we start users off with some type of badge that shows they can only handle filtered content. Users who enable viewing of offensive content replace that badge with "the good, the bad, and the ugly" badge. Something along those lines.

The idea here, is that ANY visitor to the page doesn't get presented with content that could be considered questionable for VOAT itself, or that could simply make VOAT look bad. Whether we like it or not, people are going to judge the website harshly and irresponsibly. They are going to say "VOAT" approves this content, and try to say Atko approves this content as an individual. But we can certainly make it more difficult for them to do so. With the disclaimer above, we at least know that people who would be writing the slam articles are actively looking to get offended. Once we've established that, they have even less of a basis to complain about.

Personally, I will never stop reading reddit as long as some communities there exist, such as AskScience or AskHistorians. What I'd like to do is attract those members to this community, and we have to do that with a positive and welcoming atmosphere.

We have to take PR seriously if we want VOAT to succeed long term. Absolute freedom of expression within the bounds of the law can still be had if we do this right.

Thank you for sharing this. I think that it is important to note that there were many opportunities to diffuse this whole thing if the community had chosen to. Paranoia is dangerous when unchecked. Fear is dangerous when not tempered by reason, by rational thought and empathy.

On a less abstract level, I think this video is a good example of why we should not be so hasty to throw around accusations of shills or whatnot here. Evaluate behavior, conduct, and remark upon that - separate from the person. Because what may appear as malicious intent might very well be a misunderstanding, or someone who just happens to have different views than your own.

It's this sort of divide-and-conquer strategy which is even more effective for disrupting communities than any amount of covert shilling or disinformation. Assuming good faith and evaluating behaviors for their merit seems to me to be the sensible approach.
